name: Auxiliares Raetobarii

abilities.name: Barbarian Testudo
abilities.text: The troops of this unit raise their shields above their heads in a static defensive formation.

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

abilities.name: Spear Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into close wall formation.

abilities.name: Square
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close square formation. Note that it cannot move whilst this ability is active.

attributes.name: Snipe
attributes.text: This unit remains hidden while firing.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (scrub & forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in scrub and forest until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

attributes.name: Impetuous
attributes.text: This unit gets an extra morale bonus when eager.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

short: The name Raetobarii is a tribal one, derived from one of the Alemannic tribes. This name may have been influenced by the province of Raetia, where they inhabited. Auxilia (latin) - an auxiliary unit of the Roman army. There is a strong opinion that auxilia units consisted of barbarians-volunteers, the conditions of service of which were determined by a special agreement. For instance, Vegetius directly mentions that the legions were composed of Roman citizens, and the auxilia of barbarians. Vegetius divides the barbarians themselves into «allies» and «Foederati». If under the second we can understand the representatives of tribes with whom a special pact (foedus) was concluded, the first, apparently, should include the tribes, originally or for quite a long time living on the territory of the Empire. About the internal organisation of the auxilia nothing is definitely known, but most likely, the structure of these units in the 4th century was no different from the legions. While the legions were composed of forcefully conscripted Romanised barbarians who lived on the territory of the Empire, in the auxilia served mainly volunteers from the Germanic tribes beyond the Rhine. Such system led to the fact that the auxiliaries became superior to the legionnaires in terms of their combat qualities. In the 4th century it was a recognised fact that the more barbaric was the detachment, the higher was its combat value; the process of steady enhancement of auxiliary troops, which lasted for centuries, came to an end in this era - auxilia came to be considered more capable and reliable than legions.
history: A Germanic people consisting of several confederated tribes, it is thought that the Goths came from the Baltic coast region of northern Poland, possibly incorporating land as far afield as Sweden. They began to appear on the fringes of the Roman Empire during the 3rd century AD, their migration possibly forced by overpopulation and climate changes during the Dark Ages that made agriculture difficult in their homelands. Descending into the Balkan Peninsula via Dacia and Greece, they sacked several prominent cities in the region and probably destroyed the Temple of Artemis, one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. Gothic aggression was eventually checked by the Emperor Claudius II; a deal was struck which allowed them to remain settled on the borders of Rome's empire, in Dacia, in return for military assistance as auxiliaries and foederati. This state of affairs persisted for quite some time, with the Goths converting to Arian Christianity, and even becoming somewhat Romanised in the intervening years. However, around AD370, clashes with the Sarmatians, Alans and other steppe peoples, all under pressure from the newly-arrived, marauding Huns, turned the Goths into refugees, once again bringing them into conflict with the Roman Empire.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
